AnalysisStatus.description:
Outcome of one product analysis run (§14, P6-T06).

Recorded even when it fails: §15 requires the prompt key and version of
every call, and a failed call is exactly the one someone will want to
explain later.
AnalysisStatus.title: AnalysisStatus

AnalyticsResponse.description: §99's four numbers: volume, success rate, cost, failure rate.
AnalyticsResponse.title: AnalyticsResponse

ApiInfo.description: What this API version is and what it can currently do.
ApiInfo.title: ApiInfo

product_id.description: The product to instantiate against (§57). Required: a template applied without one would be the same video every time.
product_id.title: Product Id

AspectRatio.description:
Frame shape. Stored as an enum rather than a free string because the
render pipeline (PHASE 13) resolves it to exact pixel dimensions, and
"9 : 16" versus "9:16" would be two products' worth of bugs.
AspectRatio.title: AspectRatio

AssetType.description: What kind of media an asset holds (§10.17).
AssetType.title: AssetType

BatchStatus.description:
Where a bulk import has got to (§98, P21-T04).

`VALIDATING` and `READY` are distinct from `RUNNING` because §98 asks for a
validation *preview*: the rows are parsed and checked before anybody
commits to generating dozens of videos, and a batch that went straight from
upload to running would spend money on rows a person would have rejected.
BatchStatus.title: BatchStatus

BlueprintSlot.description: One shot's shape, before a product fills it in (§57).
BlueprintSlot.title: BlueprintSlot

BrandTone.description:
How a brand speaks (§58).

§58 is explicit that a Brand Kit is not a logo uploader — it must reach
creative, script, prompt, subtitles and the ending. Tone is the part that
reaches the *words*, so it is a field rather than a note, and the generator
receives it as an instruction rather than as decoration.
BrandTone.title: BrandTone

CapabilityResponse.description: §140's schema, as the admin sees it (P19-T02).

durations.description: Exact lengths offered. Empty means continuous up to the maximum.
durations.title: Durations

CapabilityResponse.title: CapabilityResponse

ClaimRiskLevel.description:
How much substantiation a claim needs before it is safe to broadcast.

Recorded per claim so the review UI can order the queue by consequence:
an unverified `HIGH` claim about infant safety deserves attention before a
`LOW` one about colour.
ClaimRiskLevel.title: ClaimRiskLevel

ClaimStatus.description:
Whether a claim may be used (§10.8).

§109 is unambiguous: only `VERIFIED` claims reach a script.
ClaimStatus.title: ClaimStatus

ClaimType.description:
What a marketing claim asserts (§10.8).

Not enumerated by the taskbook. The split is by *what would have to be
true* for the claim to be honest, because that is what decides whether it
needs a verified fact behind it (§13, §109).
ClaimType.title: ClaimType

CostEstimateResponse.description: A quote, and whether the workspace can cover it (P18-T07).

affordable.description: Whether `maximum` fits in the available balance right now.
affordable.title: Affordable

expected.description: What this is likely to cost.
expected.title: Expected

maximum.description: What will be reserved. Higher than `expected` because providers round up and a retry costs again.
maximum.title: Maximum

CostEstimateResponse.title: CostEstimateResponse

verify.description: Confirm the fact as you create it. Only honoured for facts a user supplied — AI-sourced facts are always AI_INFERRED (§13).
verify.title: Verify

risk_notes.description: Where the model flagged something a human should check before filming — a claim it wanted and did not have, or a direction resting on something unstated (§16).
risk_notes.title: Risk Notes

available.description: What a new job may be charged against.
available.title: Available

reserved.description: The part already promised to jobs in flight.
reserved.title: Reserved

amount.description: Always positive; the type says which way it moved.
amount.title: Amount

CreditTransactionType.description:
Why credits moved (§10.29, PHASE 18).

Reserve, capture and release are three separate rows rather than one
mutated balance, because §95's acceptance — no double charge, no negative
balance, no charge on failure — is only checkable if each step left a
record. A single `balance` column can be wrong; a ledger that disagrees
with its own sum cannot hide.
CreditTransactionType.title: CreditTransactionType

DependencyStatus.description: Result of a single readiness probe.
DependencyStatus.title: DependencyStatus

DownloadResponse.description: A time-limited link to the finished video (§60).

url.description: Presigned URL. Expires; do not store it.
url.title: Url

DownloadResponse.title: DownloadResponse

ErrorCode.description: The complete set of error codes (§65).
ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

details.description: Optional structured context. Never contains secrets.
details.title: Details

message.description: Human-readable, safe to display to a user.
message.title: Message

request_id.description: Correlates this response with the server logs.
request_id.title: Request Id

ErrorResponse.description: Uniform error envelope returned by every failing endpoint.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

FactSourceType.description:
Where a fact came from (§10.7).

Distinct from :class:`VerificationStatus`, which is how much it is
trusted. A fact can be `AI_VISION` in origin and `VERIFIED` in status —
that is precisely the review workflow §13 describes — but the origin is
never overwritten, so "a human confirmed something the AI guessed" stays
distinguishable from "a human typed it in".
FactSourceType.title: FactSourceType

FactType.description:
What kind of thing a product fact asserts (§10.7).

The taskbook names ``fact_type`` without enumerating it. These values are
chosen so that the *risky* categories are separable: §13's forbidden
example ("除甲醛率 99.9%") is a `PERFORMANCE` fact, and being able to
identify that class by type is what lets the claim rules treat it more
strictly than, say, a colour.
FactType.title: FactType

idempotency_key.description: Required. A grant has no natural id, so this key is the only thing between a retried purchase webhook and a doubled balance.
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

progress.description: 0-100, advisory. Most providers report coarsely or not at all, and a smooth bar over work we cannot see would be a lie.
progress.title: Progress

JobStatus.description:
§106's job machine.

`SUBMITTED` and `PROCESSING` are distinct on purpose: the first means a
provider accepted the request, the second that it reports work underway.
Losing the distinction would make "the provider never answered" and "the
provider is slow" the same incident.
JobStatus.title: JobStatus

JobType.description:
What a job is for (§10.15).

One table for every long task, because §22 routes them all through the same
orchestrator. The type picks the queue and the worker, not the schema.
JobType.title: JobType

LogoPosition.description: Where a logo sits when one is burned in (§58, §34).
LogoPosition.title: LogoPosition

MediaAssetDetailResponse.description: An asset plus a short-lived URL to fetch it (§110).
MediaAssetDetailResponse.title: MediaAssetDetailResponse

MediaAssetResponse.description:
An asset as the client sees it.

Deliberately does **not** expose `bucket` or `object_key`. Those are
infrastructure: revealing them tells a client where files live and invites
code that constructs storage paths instead of asking for a signed URL.
MediaAssetResponse.title: MediaAssetResponse

size_bytes.description: The file's size as the client sees it. Checked again against the stored object at completion — this is an early rejection, not the authoritative limit.
size_bytes.title: Size Bytes

PresignResponse.description: Instructions for the browser's direct-to-storage PUT.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the URL stops working.
expires_in.title: Expires In

headers.description: Headers that must accompany the PUT. They are part of the signature, so omitting or changing one makes storage reject the upload.
headers.title: Headers

upload_url.description: Presigned URL. Send the file body here with PUT.
upload_url.title: Upload Url

PresignResponse.title: PresignResponse

PreviewResponse.description: What an import would do, before it does it (P21-T03).

missing_columns.description: Required columns absent from the file. Fatal for the whole import.
missing_columns.title: Missing Columns

unknown_columns.description: Columns the importer does not understand. Reported rather than ignored — a misspelled header is silently dropped data otherwise.
unknown_columns.title: Unknown Columns

PreviewResponse.title: PreviewResponse

prompt_key.description: Which registered prompt produced this result (§15).
prompt_key.title: Prompt Key

ProductAssetRole.description:
What a product image shows (§10.6).

The role is not decoration: PHASE 8's prompt compiler picks reference
imagery by role, so "the front of the product" has to be answerable
without a human looking at the picture.
ProductAssetRole.title: ProductAssetRole

status.description: Only VERIFIED claims may be used in a generated script (§109).

verification_status.description: Only VERIFIED facts may back a claim or reach a generated script (§13). Anything the AI produced is AI_INFERRED until a person confirms it.

ProductStatus.description:
Where a product sits in its lifecycle (§104).

Transitions are validated by :func:`can_transition_product`; §105 forbids
writing a status by assignment, and the same rule is applied here.
ProductStatus.title: ProductStatus

ProjectPurpose.description:
What the video is for (§10.9, §16).

Feeds the creative prompt, so these are not cosmetic: a launch film and a
marketplace listing want different structures from the same product.
ProjectPurpose.title: ProjectPurpose

ProjectStatus.description:
Where a video project has got to (§10.9, §105).

Longer than the product's machine because a project *is* the pipeline: each
state names a stage that can fail on its own and be resumed on its own.
ProjectStatus.title: ProjectStatus

active.description: Whether this is the version now being sent.
active.title: Active

circuit_open_until.description: Set by the breaker, not by an operator. Null means closed.
circuit_open_until.title: Circuit Open Until

quality_score.description: 0.0-1.0 from §37's checks over the last 30 days (§101). 1.0 when nothing has been judged — unknown reads as good, so a newly enabled provider is tried rather than buried.
quality_score.title: Quality Score

QCCheckType.description:
§37's two families.

`TECHNICAL` is decidable — a file either decodes or it does not. `VISUAL`
is a model's opinion, and §37.2 exists because the technical checks pass
happily on a video of the wrong product.
QCCheckType.title: QCCheckType

QCStatus.description:
The outcome of one quality check.

`WARNING` is distinct from `FAILED` on purpose: a clip two frames short of
its target is worth showing a person and not worth blocking a delivery on,
and collapsing the two would force every borderline result to be either
ignored or fatal.
QCStatus.title: QCStatus

QualityMode.description:
Cost/quality tier (§10.9, §138). Drives provider and model selection in
PHASE 19 and the credit price in PHASE 18.
QualityMode.title: QualityMode

ReferenceRole.description:
Why an image is attached to a shot (§10.14).

`IDENTITY` is the load-bearing one: those are the frames §29 says the
generated product must match, and PHASE 14's QC compares against exactly
this set.
ReferenceRole.title: ReferenceRole

burn_subtitles.description: Burn the subtitle track into the picture (§31).
burn_subtitles.title: Burn Subtitles

RenderStartedResponse.description: What a composition request returns: the render row and the job to poll.
RenderStartedResponse.title: RenderStartedResponse

RenderStatus.description: Where one render attempt has got to (§34).
RenderStatus.title: RenderStatus

ReorderShots.description: P20-T02. The new order, as clip indices into the VIDEO track.
ReorderShots.title: ReorderShots

RerenderRequest.description:
Nothing to configure yet. Present so adding a field is not a breaking
change from a body-less POST.
RerenderRequest.title: RerenderRequest

ReviseScriptRequest.description:
A human's edit. Validated against §17's schema like any generated one —
a hand-written script with eight sections would break PHASE 8 exactly as a
generated one would.
ReviseScriptRequest.title: ReviseScriptRequest

row_number.description: The line in the source file, header included.
row_number.title: Row Number

ScriptDocument.description:
A complete script (§17).

All nine sections, in §17's order, no duplicates. Order is not cosmetic —
PHASE 8 turns this sequence into shots, and a script whose CTA precedes its
hook would produce a storyboard nobody could film.
ScriptDocument.title: ScriptDocument

sourced_claim_ids.description: The VERIFIED claims that were in scope when this was written (P7-T09). A claim withdrawn later can be traced to every script that used it.
sourced_claim_ids.title: Sourced Claim Ids

ScriptSection.description: One narrated beat of the script (§17).
ScriptSection.title: ScriptSection

ScriptStatus.description:
§10.11. A script is DRAFT until a person accepts it.

`SUPERSEDED` rather than deletion: §17 requires history to survive an edit,
so a new version marks the old one superseded instead of overwriting it.
ScriptStatus.title: ScriptStatus

SetLogo.description: P20-T07. §141 says a missing logo must never block a render.
SetLogo.title: SetLogo

SetSubtitleStyle.description:
P20-T04. Style is metadata on the SUBTITLE track, not free-form text.

A closed set of fields rather than a style string, because the value ends
up inside ffmpeg's `force_style` argument (§35) and a string a user typed
there is an injection into the filter grammar.
SetSubtitleStyle.title: SetSubtitleStyle

SetTrackGain.description: P20-T05 and P20-T06 — one operation, because they are one thing.
SetTrackGain.title: SetTrackGain

identity_lock.description: §29's product identity lock. When on, the compiler adds the consistency rules and QC checks generated frames against the identity references below.
identity_lock.title: Identity Lock

visual_prompt.description: Compiled by the prompt compiler from this shot's fields (§19). Read-only: edit the fields and it is rebuilt.
visual_prompt.title: Visual Prompt

ShotStatus.description:
Where a shot sits in generation (§10.13).

`PENDING` means "written but never sent to a provider"; `READY` means a
generated clip has been chosen for it. The middle states become meaningful
in PHASE 9 when the job system can actually report progress.
ShotStatus.title: ShotStatus

ShotType.description:
What a shot is doing (§10.13).

Not decoration: PHASE 8's compiler picks reference imagery by shot type,
and PHASE 14's QC weights the identity check differently for a `MACRO`
than for a `LIFESTYLE` — one is mostly product, the other mostly room.
ShotType.title: ShotType

StartBatchRequest.description: Nothing configurable yet; `max_concurrency` is set at import.
StartBatchRequest.title: StartBatchRequest

StoryboardStatus.description:
§10.12. Same shape as `ScriptStatus`, and for the same reason (§17):
a new storyboard supersedes rather than overwrites, so "which storyboard
did we film" keeps an answer.
StoryboardStatus.title: StoryboardStatus

TargetPlatform.description: Where the video will be published (§10.9).
TargetPlatform.title: TargetPlatform

TemplateBlueprint.description: A template's whole shot plan, validated as one thing (§57).
TemplateBlueprint.title: TemplateBlueprint

edited.description: True once operations have been applied to the composed cut.
edited.title: Edited

TokenResponse.description:
Issued credentials.

The refresh token is **not** in this body — it is set as an HttpOnly cookie.
Returning it here would put a long-lived credential somewhere JavaScript
can read it.
TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse

TransitionType.description:
How a shot enters or leaves (§10.13). Resolved to ffmpeg filters in
PHASE 13; kept as an enum because "cross fade" and "crossfade" would be two
products' worth of render bugs.
TransitionType.title: TransitionType

TrimClip.description:
P20-T03. Shorten or lengthen one clip's slot on the timeline.

`source_start_ms` moves the in-point *within* the generated clip; changing
it is how a trim keeps the interesting part rather than always the first
seconds.
TrimClip.title: TrimClip

UpdateBrandKitRequest.description: Every field optional. Absent means unchanged, not cleared.
UpdateBrandKitRequest.title: UpdateBrandKitRequest

verify.description: Re-confirm after editing. Without it, changing a value drops the fact back to USER_PROVIDED, because whatever was verified before was a different statement.
verify.title: Verify

UpdateShotRequest.description:
Everything a user may change about a shot.

Note the absence of `visual_prompt` and `negative_prompt` — see the module
docstring. Their absence is the enforcement.
UpdateShotRequest.title: UpdateShotRequest

UploadConfigResponse.description:
What this deployment accepts.

Served so the file picker and the validator agree by construction. A
hardcoded client-side list drifts from the server's and turns a policy
change into a confusing rejection after the transfer.
UploadConfigResponse.title: UploadConfigResponse

VerificationStatus.description:
How much a fact may be trusted (§10.7, §13).

This is the Truth Layer. Only `VERIFIED` facts may back a claim, and only
`VERIFIED` claims may reach a script (§109). Everything the AI produces
starts at `AI_INFERRED` and can only be promoted by a person.
VerificationStatus.title: VerificationStatus

VideoStyle.description: Visual register (§10.9). Reaches the prompt compiler in PHASE 8.
VideoStyle.title: VideoStyle

permissions.description: What the caller may do here. The UI uses this to hide actions; the server enforces it regardless (§40).
permissions.title: Permissions

role.description: The calling user's role in this workspace.
role.title: Role

WorkspaceRole.description:
Membership role (§40).

Ordered from most to least privileged; :func:`role_rank` relies on that
ordering for "at least this role" comparisons.
WorkspaceRole.title: WorkspaceRole

info.description:
HTTP API for AI Product Video Studio.

Long-running AI work (analysis, shot generation, TTS, render, QC) is **never**
performed inside a request. Those endpoints validate, create a `GenerationJob`,
enqueue it and return `202 Accepted` with a `job_id` to poll (taskbook §22).

Every failure returns the same envelope:

```json
{"error": {"code": "PROJECT_NOT_FOUND", "message": "...", "request_id": "..."}}
```

`code` comes from a closed set (§65) and is the field clients should branch on.
info.title: AI Product Video Studio API

get.description:
Describe this API version.

Reports which feature flags are on so a client can adapt without probing
endpoints that are deliberately disabled.

§99's acceptance: 生成量, 成功率, 成本, 失败率 (P22-T07, P22-T08).

Computed with aggregates rather than by loading jobs and counting in
Python. The difference does not matter at a thousand jobs and decides
whether this page loads at a million.
get.summary: Generation volume, success rate and cost

get.description:
§99's job monitor (P22-T03).

Cross-tenant, which is why this router is guarded by platform admin rather
than by a workspace role.

schema.title: Response List Jobs Api V1 Admin Jobs Get

get.description:
§99's failure view (P22-T04).

Separate from `/jobs?status=FAILED` because it also covers `TIMEOUT`, and
because a time bound is the difference between a page that loads and one
that scans a year of history.

schema.title: Response List Failed Jobs Api V1 Admin Jobs Failed Get

get.description:
§15's registry, every version (P22-T06).

Read-only, and that is the design rather than an omission. §15 makes a
version immutable: a job records the key and version it sent, and an
endpoint that could edit that text would let someone change what a recorded
call *claims* to have sent. Shipping a new prompt is a deploy, which leaves
a commit; editing one through an API would not.

Superseded versions are listed alongside the active one, because the
question this view answers is usually "what did that job actually send",
and the answer is often not the current text.

schema.title: Response List Prompts Api V1 Admin Prompts Get

get.description:
§54's config with §55's observed health folded in (P19-T04, P22-T05).

One endpoint rather than two, because the only question anyone asks here is
"which of these is working" — and answering it from two screens means
reading a config that says enabled next to a health page that says failing.

schema.title: Response List Providers Api V1 Admin Providers Get

get.description:
§140's matrix (P19-T02).

Read from code rather than the database: capabilities change when a vendor
ships a model, and a row an operator could edit would let someone claim a
provider does 7-second clips when it does not.

schema.title: Response List Capabilities Api V1 Admin Providers Capabilities Get

post.description:
§54's switch (P19-T07).

Enabling also clears the breaker: someone turning a provider back on means
"try this again now", and leaving a breaker open would make the switch
appear to do nothing.

get.description:
§99's user list (P22-T02).

Workspaces rather than users, because usage and cost are billed to a
workspace and a user in three of them is three different customers.

schema.title: Response List Workspaces Api V1 Admin Workspaces Get

get.summary: Workspaces and what they have spent

post.description:
Exchange email and password for tokens.

Every failure returns the same error regardless of cause, and the
no-such-user path still performs a password hash, so neither the response
nor its timing reveals whether an email is registered.

Revoke the refresh token and clear the cookie.

Succeeds even without a valid token: a logout that fails leaves the user
believing they are signed out when they are not.

get.description: Return the authenticated user.

post.description:
Rotate the refresh token and issue a new access token.

The presented token is revoked as part of the exchange, so a stolen one is
usable at most once.

Register a user and their personal workspace, then sign them in.

A user without a workspace cannot use the product at all, so both are
created in one transaction.

get.description: Every workspace the caller belongs to. Never any others.

schema.title: Response List Workspaces Api V1 Workspaces Get

post.description: Create a workspace. The caller becomes its OWNER.

get.description:
Fetch one workspace.

Returns 404 — not 403 — when the caller is not a member, so workspace ids
cannot be probed for existence across tenants.
Finished assets in this workspace, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Assets Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Assets Get

get.description: One asset, with a short-lived signed URL to fetch its bytes.
get.summary: Get one asset with a download URL

schema.title: Response List Batches Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Batches Get

post.description:
Create the batch and its items (P21-T04).

Invalid rows are stored as `INVALID` items rather than dropped, so the
count a user sees matches the file they uploaded.
post.summary: Import a spreadsheet as a batch

post.description:
§98's validation preview (P21-T03).

Writes nothing. Every row's verdict is returned so a user can fix their
spreadsheet before committing to generating dozens of videos.
post.summary: Validate a spreadsheet without importing it

post.description:
Stop a batch. Rows already running are left to finish — interrupting a
generation mid-flight wastes what has already been paid for.

get.description: §98's per-item status (P21-T06). `row_number` is the source line.

schema.title: Response List Items Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Batches  Batch Id  Items Get

post.description:
P21-T07. Retries `FAILED` rows only.

`INVALID` rows are not retried: their row is wrong, and running it again
produces the same wrong row. Those need a corrected file.

Queue the first tranche (P21-T05).

Only up to `max_concurrency` items are claimed here; the worker claims the
next as each finishes. Queuing all five hundred at once would fill every
queue with one tenant's work, which is exactly what P21-T08 forbids.

schema.title: Response List Brand Kits Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Brand Kits Get

delete.description:
Soft-delete. Projects made under this kit keep their reference, because
"which brand was this video made under" is asked about shipped videos.

get.description:
The workspace's balance (P18-T08).

Creates the account on first read rather than 404ing. A workspace that has
never generated anything has no account row, and "you have no account" is a
worse answer than "you have your signup grant".

post.description:
Top up a workspace. `BILLING_MANAGE` — owners only (§40).

Audited as a `CREDIT_ADJUSTMENT` (§60): moving money is the category of
action a trail exists for.

get.description:
The ledger, newest first (P18-T08).

Every movement, including reservations that were released. A history that
showed only charges would leave a user unable to explain why their
available balance dipped during a generation that failed.

schema.title: Response List Transactions Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Credits Transactions Get

get.description: §26's polling endpoint. The frontend calls this every few seconds.

post.description:
Stop a job.

A job that already finished is returned unchanged rather than erroring: the
user wanted it stopped and it is stopped, and raising over a race they
cannot see would be pedantry.

schema.title: Response List Members Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Members Get

post.description:
Add an existing user. Requires `member:invite`.

Granting OWNER additionally requires `member:update_role`, so an admin
cannot escalate by inviting an account they control as an owner.

delete.description:
Remove a member, or leave the workspace yourself.

Leaving needs no permission; removing someone else requires
`member:remove`. Removing the last owner is refused either way.

patch.description:
Change a role. Requires `member:update_role` (OWNER only).

Demoting the last owner is refused: a workspace with no owner cannot be
billed, deleted, or have its membership managed.

schema.title: Response List Products Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Products Get

post.description: Create a product. Always starts in DRAFT (§104).

patch.description:
Edit descriptive fields.

`status` is deliberately not editable here — §105 forbids arbitrary status
writes, so transitions go through their own endpoints.

schema.title: Response List Analyses Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Products  Product Id  Analyses Get

post.description:
Run vision analysis and file the results for review (§14).

Everything the model observes lands as an `AI_INFERRED` fact and everything
it suggests lands as a `SUGGESTED` claim — nothing here is publishable, and
the product moves to `REVIEW_REQUIRED` rather than to a ready state.

Synchronous for now, which §83 permits at this length. PHASE 9 moves it
behind the job queue, at which point this returns the analysis in `PENDING`
and the client polls.

schema.title: Response List Product Assets Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Products  Product Id  Assets Get

post.description:
Attach an already-uploaded media asset (§10.6).

The first image attached becomes the primary one automatically.
post.summary: Attach an image to a product

delete.description: Detach an image. The underlying file is untouched (§163 reclaims it).

schema.title: Response List Claims Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Products  Product Id  Claims Get

post.description: Propose a marketing claim. Always created SUGGESTED (§10.8).

get.description:
§109's `get_verified_claims`, exposed over HTTP.

A separate route rather than a query parameter, so "the claims that may be
broadcast" is a distinct thing a caller asks for rather than a filter it
has to remember to apply.

schema.title: Response List Verified Claims Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Products  Product Id  Claims Verified Get

post.description:
Approve a claim (§13, §109).

Refused with `CLAIM_NOT_VERIFIED` when the claim asserts something
checkable and cites no verified fact. Only EMOTIONAL claims — which assert
nothing substantiable — are exempt.

schema.title: Response List Facts Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Products  Product Id  Facts Get

post.description:
Record something true about the product (§10.7).

Facts created here are `USER_INPUT`: this endpoint is a person typing.
The analyser's AI-sourced facts go through the same service and are forced
to `AI_INFERRED` (§13) — there is no route that can create a verified AI
fact.

patch.description:
Edit a fact, optionally re-confirming it.

Changing the value withdraws any prior verification and sends claims that
cited it back for review — they were approved against a different
statement.

post.description:
Mark a fact wrong.

Any verified claim that cited it is demoted to SUGGESTED in the same
transaction — evidence withdrawn means the sentence built on it is no
longer approved.

Take responsibility for a fact (§13).

Records who confirmed it and when. This is the only way a fact becomes
usable as evidence.

Move a product to READY.

Refused unless at least one fact has been verified: a product with nothing
confirmed has nothing a script could truthfully say (§13).

schema.title: Response List Projects Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Projects Get

post.description: Create a project against a product. Always starts in DRAFT (§105).

patch.description:
Change the brief, while the project is still ahead of generation.

Refused afterwards: changing the duration once shots exist would silently
invalidate work already paid for. Move the project back a stage first.

get.description:
§95's pre-generation quote (P18-T07).

Estimated from the approved storyboard's actual shot durations when one
